reason: While the text clearly depicts Yahweh as all-powerful through extensive descriptions of divine might—'The Lord is a man of war,' control over the sea and winds, 'awesome in splendor'—it directly contradicts the 'remote' characterization. The dominant theological emphasis is Yahweh's intimate engagement: personal relationship ('This is my God'), steadfast love ('You led the people whom you redeemed in your hesitant love'), direct active intervention ('You brought them in and planted them'), and reciprocal worship ('I will exalt him'). The text presents a transcendent yet immanently involved God, not a remote one.
